baseline.integratorAssessment: programmer-art tier (~5): fallback serif fonts, debug vectors on by default, flat circles for asteroids, touch pads always visible on desktop, flat rectangles for lunar surface and pad, painted 1280px planets mismatched with pixel ship, no audio.

strengths: Massive improvement over the baseline: every placeholder grey circle and debug overlay is gone, and all art loads with zero fallbacks.
Palette is on-brand: cosmos #17182D base, plum nebula, sage/cream Tea Moon, amber/orange accents that match design-system tokens.
Asteroid cast has real personality (sleepy face, mossy tea rock, mochi, rice). They feel cozy and handcrafted, not hazardous-generic.
Tea Moon destination is a genuine hero moment: the teacup crater, tiny tea house with steam and soft stepped halo read instantly as 'deliver here'.

Huge leap from baseline: no debug HUD, no vector placeholder circles, and no fallback textures. The palette (navy cosmos, cream, orange accent, sage/plum) matches colors_and_type.css and design-system tokens.
Hero ship now renders crisp at an integer 2x when axis-aligned (flight-start/cruise). The round-1 0.72 non-integer smear is fixed.
Asteroids are characterful, consistently 2x pixel art with good silhouettes and cozy faces. Planets are now opaque, so the round-1 ghosting is fixed.

Tea Moon destination is a strong focal point: cottage, smoke, teacup crater, stepped halo. The gate language (dashed orange ring, then a cream progress arc over sage dashes, a chevron, a status chip) reads clearly.

openIssues: [major] (flight-environment (FlightScene HUD layout) / ui) The phone-landscape compact HUD drops two pieces of essential live data: the bottom-side heading and the package condition. ui-reference 'Flight HUD' lists both as required overlays, and the bottom heading is the core docking mechanic. On keyboard phoneLandscape the control-hint footer also vanishes, so a player has no on-screen key reference.

[major] (flight-environment) On the touch layout the gate status pill ('hold steady...') is anchored at moon-relative world space and slides under the brake touch pad. The text is clipped and overlaps an interactive control right at the most important moment (the arrival window).

[minor] (flight-environment / assets) Parallax depth is flat. Background planets and foreground asteroids use the same pixel density, saturation and contrast and overlap freely: the cheese asteroid is stacked on Planet I'm Fine, and a rock edge peeks out behind it. The ringed planet drifts under the translucent route-note pill in every state, which competes with the note text. It reads as stickers on one plane rather than distant worlds behind a playfield.

[minor] (assets) The nebula texture is still mostly double-upscaled. In nebula.png (640x360, artScale 2) 80% of 2x2 blocks are uniform, so cloud edges step in about 4 screen-px clusters next to 2 px asteroids and stars. This is visible as chunky staircase cloud edges at the top-right and bottom.

[minor] (flight-environment / assets) The ship at arbitrary rotation (e.g. 107 degrees during approach) is nearest-neighbour rotated, producing stair-stepped jaggies along the gyoza crust and dome. In side view the gyoza silhouette reads as a croissant/baguette with a tiny dome, weakening the 'readable at small HUD size' goal from the design system.

[minor] (audio-fx) A smooth anti-aliased radial glow sits at the nozzle beside the pixel flame and trail, mixing vector softness into the pixel FX. The thrust trail is also very long (about 350 px) and ruler-straight, reading as a rocket jet rather than cozy puffs.

[nit] (flight-environment) The ghost target silhouette in the gate is a dithered blob with knobby protrusions that reads as a puzzle piece or cat rather than the ship. The chevron disc sits on the moon limb and covers the moon art.

[nit] (assets) Debris rocks are flat, low-contrast grey-green lumps with no highlight or character. They read as filler or near-placeholder next to the expressive asteroids, and the green-grey sits outside the warm/plum palette.

[nit] (flight-environment / audio-fx) The bump hit-flash floods both the ship and the asteroid with flat white or cream, erasing all interior detail (face, dome, pleats) for the flash duration. It looks like a missing texture in a still frame.

strengths: Huge visual leap over baseline: cohesive dusk palette (plum/navy sky, peach planet, cream ground, terracotta/sage accents) that matches colors_and_type.css warmth
Diegetic landing site: striped blanket on trestles, lanterns that light sequentially on touchdown, cottage with chimney smoke, rabbit NPC who waves on soft landing - strong cozy storytelling
Copy voice is on-brand: lowercase, warm, funny low-stakes failure lines ('moon blanket says: softer, please', 'Emotionally rotated')
Parchment result card with state dot + retry progress bar reads clearly on desktop and matches the UI kit
Huge leap over the baseline: a full handcrafted Tea Moon diorama (sky gradient, hills, banded planet, steaming cottage, waving rabbit, lanterns, striped blanket pad) on one consistent 2 px pixel grid
Upright ship redraw at 64x80@2x is crisp, readable and charming; it matches the pixel density of the scenery
HUD follows the design system: dark 0.78 panel, pixel-font gold header, mono rows, ember/amber state colouring, gentle flavour copy ('emotionally rotated', 'slightly shaken')
Live speed gauge with soft/bumpy/too-fast bands and a state pill gives clear, cozy landing feedback

openIssues: [major] (assets + landing (ShipSprite / LandingScene)) Tilted, incident and off-pad ship poses are rotated off the pixel grid with nearest sampling, so the outline and dome ring turn ragged with 1 px stair-steps. Tilting is the core landing verb, so this shows on screen most of the time and is now the one place the 2 px pixel contract breaks.

[minor] (landing (HUD) / ui) The dashboard chatter line is truncated with an ellipsis, so the joke's punchline is lost: 'please apply soup-facing thr…' (full: '…thrust') and 'gyro humming, dumpling level…'.

[minor] (landing (HUD)) After an incident the HUD contradicts what the player sees. It shows 'tilt level 5°' and 'level 10°' while the dumpling lies tipped or on its side, and 'drift steady 1.7 m/s ←' after the crash. On phone, the off-pad cue 'find the pad' lives only in the altitude row, which the compact HUD hides.

[minor] (landing (scenery / aids)) The landing guide beam is a stack of flat translucent rectangles with a hard horizontal top edge floating in the sky. It reads as placeholder geometry rather than a painted light, and it washes the hills behind the pad.
[minor] (landing (scenery / camera)) Incident camera shake exposes a 2 px wrapped column of the right-edge planet (orange and pink) at the far left edge of the screen.

[minor] (audio-fx / landing) In the success hero moment, touchdown dust puffs draw in front of the ship and cover its legs and lower hull. The dumpling reads as sunk into cotton right when the featherlight card appears.

[minor] (landing (aids)) The stabilizer level guides are free-floating thin green dashes beside the ship. On desktop the right dash is hidden behind the speed gauge, so a lone green line hangs in the sky and looks like a debug marker.
[nit] (landing (scenery stars) / ui) The sky sparkle '+' star shows through the 0.78 HUD panel right in the 'drift' row, where it reads like a stray glyph or icon in the data table.
[nit] (audio-fx) The thrust plume is a long, bent, dark-streaked orange column (~120 px) that reads more like a churro or rope trail than a cozy nozzle flame.
[nit] (landing (touch HUD) / ui) The touch layout has no retry control, while keyboard players get 'R retry'. The thrust and steady tile stack also abuts the cottage edge.

[nit] (e2e harness) The playtest retry metric (retrySeconds 3.37) is measured from key release, so it includes the free-fall before the crash. That overstates the retry time against the < 2.5 s target, even though the actual incident-to-retry beat is 1.22 s.

strengths: Huge improvement over the baseline title: a cohesive warm-cosmos palette that matches colors_and_type.css (terracotta, sage, cream parchment, cosmos ink)
Strong typographic hierarchy: Bricolage 800 two-tone title with a warm offset shadow, a clear subtitle, and a distinct Silkscreen CTA
The parchment delivery card reads as handcrafted stationery: dotted divider, corner ticks, portrait, item tile, gentle pill. It balances well against the dominant cosmos.
Saved completion is clearly visible on title-completed: tape sticker, sage 'delivered' pill and a happy portrait swap

A real typographic hierarchy: Bricolage 800 display title with a two-tone cream/ember lockup and terracotta offset shadow, then a Bricolage tagline, Silkscreen pixel labels on buttons and section heads, mono for keycaps and data. Fonts load with no failures and the hierarchy matches design-system.md.

Parchment and cosmos are well balanced. One warm card and one ember CTA anchor a deep-cosmos field with pixel clouds, and the tea-cup moon, teahouse and dotted route trail tell the delivery story at a glance.

Saved completion is clearly visible on title-completed: CTA copy changes to 'deliver tea again', a Route Log button appears, a 'delivered · postcard collected' tab and 'delivered' pill show, and the rabbit portrait becomes happy. The Route Log modal shows the collected postcard and stats.
Corrupt-save handling is friendly and on-tone ('your old save was crumpled...'), and the probe confirms the backup was kept.

openIssues: [major] (ui builder (TitleScene composition)) The hero ship on the title is still undersized and sits on a muddy grey halo. On desktop it is about 100 px wide (about 50 px on phoneLandscape) against the design-system target of 140-180 px for the title ship. The moon (about 280 px) and the delivery card visually outrank it, so the 'large gyoza ship and title' brief from ui-reference is not met. Behind it is a stepped radial disc that lifts the background to desaturated grey (sampled (48,45,58) inside vs (21,22,41) cosmos). Its bands step in chunky ~6-8 px rings, a coarser pixel density than the 2x ship art, so it reads as a grey smudge or spotlight rather than a warm glow.

[minor] (ui builder (Button variants / TitleScene)) The secondary buttons are inconsistent. On title-completed, SETTINGS (dark navy with a heavy near-black bottom lip) and ROUTE LOG (cream parchment) sit side by side at the same hierarchy level but use different styles. The dark variant's black lip makes it read as sunken or pressed next to the raised cream button, which muddies the affordance. In the ui-kit, 'settings' at rest and 'pressed' differ only by fill darkness.

[minor] (ui builder (src/ui/Meter.ts, src/ui/layout.ts)) The settings music meter shows a phantom partial segment. At 70% it renders 7 full dusk segments plus a dim 8th one, while effects at 80% renders exactly 8. Cause: in Meter.setValue, Math.round(0.7/0.005)*0.005 = 0.7000000000000001, and segmentFills then gives the 8th segment a ~1e-15 fill, which draws at alpha 0.35+.

[minor] (ui builder (TitleScene delivery card)) The completion tab looks bolted on. 'delivered · postcard collected' is a separate sage strip with a drop shadow, floating above and overlapping the card's top border at the right edge, with a ✦ sparkle colliding at its corner. On phoneLandscape it crowds the ship trail and the moon's lower edge. The card already says 'delivered' in its pill, so the information is duplicated in two styles.

[minor] (ui builder (compact layout tokens)) Small text and wrapping at phone size. On phoneLandscape the footer 'handmade slice · ofl type', the settings 'saved on this device' and hint row, and the route-log stat labels render at about 7 px. The item chip wraps 'hot tea and moon / mochi' with an orphan word, and the teapot sprite overhangs the chip's left border. The corrupt-save notice wraps to two lines and nearly touches the footer.

[nit] (integrator (scale config) / ui builder) Canvas pillarboxing on phone landscape. The 16:9 canvas leaves about 70 px dark bars on each side of an 844x390 screen, about 18% of the width, even though the compact title layout would comfortably use the full width.

[nit] (asset producer (icons)) Icon readability. The teacup icon's steam is drawn as navy/white checker pixels, so on the ember CTA it reads as dark grit rather than steam. In the ui-kit, the gyoza icon (2nd in row 1) reads as a spotted cookie or acorn rather than a pleated dumpling.

[nit] (ui builder (UiKitScene)) The ui-kit gallery leaves out components that ship on the title. The settings toggle switch, -/+ stepper keys, modal shell with dotted header, route-log postcard row, completion tab, notice pill (corrupt save) and rotate-prompt card are not shown. The disabled button is labeled 'RESTING', which reads as a rest state rather than disabled. Bottom padding in the middle and left columns is tight, with the parchment footer about 5 px from the panel edge.

[nit] (ui builder (TitleScene scenery)) The moon's surrounding halo is a faint dark ring that dims the nebula clouds next to it. It reads as a shadow cutout rather than a glow, which runs against the warm, cozy direction.

strengths: Audio engine is architecturally excellent: a pure, exhaustive GameEvent mapper (audioCues.ts) separated from Web Audio rendering, all tuning in typed data, and a unit-test file present (tests/audioCues.test.ts).

Gesture-gated AudioContext verified live: 'uncreated' before input, 'running' after a pointer click. Keydown, pointerdown and touchend all unlock. The context suspends and resumes with tab visibility.

Robust mastering chain (glue compressor, then limiter, then tanh soft-clip at -1 dBFS). Offline analysis shows the stacked worst case (result music + thrust + dramatic bump + incident + touchdown + chime) peaking at only -3.6 dBFS, with no clipping and no NaNs.
Graceful failure everywhere: handleEvent, the scheduler, loops and sfx are all try/catch-wrapped, there is a webkit fallback, and nothing runs (silent no-op) until a gesture unlocks the context.
Round-1 FX majors resolved: the landing nozzle flame is now pixel tongue frames at integer 2x, with no anti-aliased triangle or banded radial disc
Particle pixel density now matches the 2x ship and scenery, and particles pop out fully opaque, with no grey alpha mush over navy
Dust no longer shows charcoal tail frames. Cream, gold and ember palette is warm and cohesive with the Tea Moon art
Flight bump feedback reads well: hard tint flash on ship and rock, then a cream puff bloom between them

openIssues: [major] (flight-environment (ShipEngine), with audio-fx supplying the stepped glow helper) The flight engine glow is a smooth anti-aliased radial gradient (canvas createRadialGradient, ADD blend, non-integer scale) sitting under the pixel flame. It is the same class of defect as the round-1 nozzle-disc major, now on the most-seen FX in the game, and it contradicts ARCHITECTURE 5.6 pixel rules. The fx package already ships a hard-edged stepped glow (pixelGlowTextureKey).

[minor] (landing (LandingScene), with audio-fx tuning in fxPresets) On a soft landing, the dust bursts are drawn in front of the ship (depth.ship+1, 12-26 puffs), so cream clouds cover the saucer rim, legs and dome base at the 'featherlight landing' payoff. The gentlest landing gets the biggest cloud.

[minor] (landing (LandingScene) + audio-fx (burstIncident options)) The landing incident burst is muddled. Flour and confetti fire at depth.worldFx behind and under the tumbling ship, so the comedic poof reads as a vertical cream smear with the confetti crosses buried inside. The gallery version, a readable poof plus an upward confetti fan, does not come through in game.

[minor] (audio-fx (thrust trail tuning in fxPresets)) The landing thrust plume reads as a solid rope or tree trunk. Puffs barely spread or break up and step through orange, rust and tan in lockstep, forming a continuous column 70-100 px long from nozzle to pad. It lacks the flicker, gaps and taper that sell a cozy little burner.

[minor] (landing (LandingAids)) The stabilizer feedback is plain white and grey Graphics squares with partial alpha orbiting the ship. They read as snow or dead pixels, not a gyro effect, and are the only partial-alpha particle-like FX left, contrary to the pop-out rule.

[minor] (landing (LandingScene intro)) The landing intro braking flame is silent. The cinematic shows a burning thrust flame, but no landing:thrust event fires during the intro, so the thrust loop never plays, which breaks audio-visual coherence on the first landing beat.
[minor] (ui (installSoundToast)) In flight, the mute toast overlaps the HUD: the 'sound off [M]' toast sits on top of the top-centre chatter bar and hides half of the route note.

[minor] (audio-fx (src/data/audioCues.ts SFX_TUNING)) The bump and incident cues barely differ in loudness. bump-soft peaks at -9.4 dB and bump-dramatic at -9.5 dB (momentary -22.4 vs -20.8), and the incident is only 0.8 dB above the dramatic bump (-20.0). Severity is carried by pitch alone, so a dramatic bump does not land harder than a scrape. ui-hover sits at -48 dB momentary, about 25 dB under the music bed, and will be inaudible on laptop speakers.
[nit] (audio-fx (thrust trail tuning)) The flight thrust trail ends in tan split-puff frames that read as broken debris chunks, and at about 3 ship lengths the trail dominates the cruise composition.
[nit] (ui / landing) Background stars show through the translucent landing HUD panel: a faint '+' twinkle sits between the 'drift' label and its value.

[nit] (audio-fx (FxGalleryScene)) One gallery frame captured right after toggling reduced motion showed the hover ship sliced vertically (dome and left half missing, white sliver). It was not reproduced in 10 follow-up frames and may be a capture tear, but it is worth a glance.

strengths: Huge improvement over baseline: production rabbit portrait, item sprites, memory postcard and parchment card replace the serif placeholder text card entirely; zero fallbacks.

Result copy is outstanding and on-brief: 'a spirited delivery', 'That landing sounded like a cupboard. Very comforting, actually.', '2 friendly bumps along the way', 'landed on try 2 · the moon waited' -- warm, never shaming, backed by a banned-words list in src/data/resultCopy.ts.

Clear visual hierarchy: pixel kicker > display headline > quoted reaction > stamps > mono stats > footer actions; the palette (parchment, ink, terracotta, sage/amber pills) matches design-system.md tokens.

Navigation is explicit: labelled 'back to title [esc]' and 'fly again [enter]' buttons with keycaps; pointer taps only skip the staged reveal; event.repeat is ignored; leave() is guarded against double activation.

Huge leap from the baseline Times-New-Roman text box to a cohesive stationery card: parchment surfaces, design-system state-pill palettes, Silkscreen kicker, Bricolage headline, JetBrains Mono stats. It matches the design-system tokens and 'cozy stationery' intent.

Pixel contract on desktop is now clean. The rabbit portrait, items, stat icons, postcard and stamps all sit on an exact 2x grid with no rotation. Settled frames have no leftover particles (liveTwinkles=0).

Copy is consistently warm and funny, with no shame language. Every outcome reads as a successful delivery ('Reassembled with care. I'll eat it in the order it landed.'), and resultCopyBannedWords is enforced by tests.
Persistence states are surfaced gently and accurately. They cover the session-only footnote for newer-save / storage-unavailable / write-failed and the 'crumpled save, kept a copy' title notice.

openIssues: [minor] (ui (app shell / screens.css) with result builder) In phone portrait the result card (tiny tier) stays live under the DOM rotate overlay, and the CSS sends pointer events through to it. The canvas buttons sit under the overlay card, so a tap on the 'turn your phone sideways' card can invisibly trigger FLY AGAIN or BACK TO TITLE. That breaks the 'navigation only by explicit, visible buttons' rule. It also means the effort put into the tiny tier is never seen.

[minor] (save-results (DeliveryResultScene / resultCopy layouts)) Composition leaves a dead zone in the right column. Under the three stat rows and left of the postcard is an empty parchment block of about 370x100 px on desktop (about 330x110 on compact). The left panel also has empty bands above the portrait and below the item caption. The card reads top-heavy and the postcard looks parked in a corner rather than placed.

[minor] (save-results) Type hierarchy is crowded at the top of the copy column. The quote is bold display type at xl, almost as heavy as the headline, so the two blocks compete. Its greedy wrap also leaves one-word widows ('little gyoza.”', 'landed.”', 'comforting, actually.”'). In the incident state the headline steps down to 2xl, which moves the stamps, divider and stats up about 13 px compared with the other outcomes.

[nit] (save-results / ui kit (Button.ts)) Button language changes between tiers. Desktop uses letter-spaced Silkscreen caps with keycaps. Compact uses lowercase bold Geist with no keycaps and different proportions, so the same screen has two different button identities. The compact footer note also floats with no visual anchor.

[nit] (save-results) On phone landscape the pixel art (rabbit at portraitScale 3, postcard, items) is smooth-downsampled to about 1.6 physical px per art px. It looks soft and slightly blurred next to the crisp desktop rendering. It is acceptable and legible, but not pixel-crisp.

[nit] (save-results (SaveSystem)) When a parseable but malformed save is 'repaired', it is rewritten in place with no backup. Only unparseable or non-object JSON is backed up. A save with unknown or extra fields (e.g. from a newer patch that still says version 1), or with one malformed list, loses that data permanently on first load.

[nit] (save-results) The session-only footnote is italic Geist, which looks like a synthesized oblique. It is the only italic in the UI, and the design system defines no italic role. Small, but a little off-system.

strengths: Environment and prop art (asteroids, tea moon, teahouse, pad, lanterns, rocks, rabbit sprite and portrait, items, UI kit) is cohesive, crisp 2px pixel art with ink outlines and a warm palette that matches colors_and_type.css. It is a large improvement over the baseline.
Manifest integrity: all 47 entries exist with exact dimensions and frame strips. 0 failed assets and 0 fallbacks across all states.
Anchors are correct: the ground surface is at row 8 and the pad surface at row 6. The pad, lanterns, rabbit and teahouse sit on the surface line without floating or sinking.
Landing scene composition (dusk gradient, layered hills, warm teahouse, striped pad) reaches the cozy 'Spiritfarer-lite' bar.

Hero ship fully redrawn at true 64x80 resolution with hard alpha and integer 2x display. Clean dome ring, readable pilot, tapered flame, consistent registration across all 9 frames. It no longer reads as noise next to the asteroids and teahouse.
Nebula pixel density fixed: true-resolution art, no baked 2x2 doubling, renders at 2 screen px per art px like the stars.
Unused legacy painted planets removed. planet-far-plum, planet-im-fine and tea-moon are crisp, outlined, on-palette and opaque.

All 45 manifest entries match exact size and frames. Anchors hold: ground surface at row 8, pad surface at row 6, all sprites reach the bottom row. Provenance is recorded for every folder. Total 545 KB.

openIssues: [major] (lunar) lunar-hills-far reads as a posterized smear, not authored pixel art. It has no readable ridge silhouettes, a ragged stepped crest, blotchy dark diagonal streaks and no rim light. It fills the middle band of every landing frame, directly behind the crisp outlined teahouse, pad, lanterns and rabbit, so the clash in density and authorship is obvious.

[major] (lunar) The big ringed planet baked into lunar-sky (behind the teahouse) is a quantized painting. Its bands are noisy horizontal streaks with speckle, the rim staircase is irregular with no clean outline on the left, and the ring is broken. It sits directly behind the hero teahouse, so it draws the eye and is visibly lower craft than planet-far-plum, which is drawn in the same style family.

[minor] (space) The nebula is now true resolution, but it is still a soft, low-contrast mush with no authored cloud forms. Every pixel is partial alpha (0 opaque px), and there are fuzzy partial-alpha fringes and median-blur blobs. On the title and in flight it reads as haze rather than the 'puffy rounded clouds' brief, and it is the softest thing on screen next to the crisp asteroids.

[minor] (asteroids) asteroid-crumb has a straight 'sliced' lower-left face with no dark outline, plus a thin cream diagonal highlight strip along the cut. Every other asteroid has a continuous ink outline, so in flight this one looks cropped or broken.

[minor] (lunar) The teahouse bakes a static cream steam squiggle above its chimney. At runtime a second animated steam column is spawned about 9 art px left of the chimney, rising from the roof tiles. The result is two white wisps, one frozen and one rising from the wrong place.

[minor] (items) The memory postcard shows a different ship and moon from the hero art. The moon has no teacup crater and different greens. The ship is a flatter saucer whose trail ends in a heart-like white puff. It is the reward image, so it should picture the same ship and Tea Moon the player just flew.

[minor] (particles) Particle tails go charcoal. Frames 6-8 of thrust and frames 5-6 of dust are mid or dark grey. On the cosmos background they read as soot or ash rather than cozy steam or flour, and the dark-grey last thrust frame blends into the navy.

[nit] (ship) The ship is now the simplest sprite in the set. Its crimp creases are faint 1 px lines and the pilot face is about 6 px, so at 2x (about 104 px wide) it has less surface detail than the 150-200 px asteroids. It is also shown below the design system's 140-180 px title-hero size.

[nit] (characters) rabbit-sprite frames 0, 2 and 3 touch row 0 (ear tips), and frames 2 and 3 touch column 0 (wave sparkles). That leaves no safety margin, so the edge pixels may get clipped or bleed under filtering or trimming.
